description: task-b1 — orphaned Okta integration. A departed automation contractor (Dmitri Sokolov) left behind an over-privileged, externally-driven Okta service account (svc-scim-sync), an SSWS API token, and a rogue OIDC client-credentials app ('Access Sync Connector') that keep re-granting privileged access. Password/session/MFA resets do not stop it (an SSWS token is independent of the account's credentials and survives a mere suspend); the recurrence only stops when the token is revoked and the orphaned account is deprovisioned. Cleaning the obvious symptom is insufficient: the automation also left standing SUPER_ADMIN on a live employee (Carmen Costa) surfaced only by a privileged-access audit, the contractor's own account was only SUSPENDED (not deprovisioned), and a rogue OAuth app persists as a re-entry backdoor. The identity-automation engagement was a contractor team (Dmitri plus Marco Reyes and Priya Nair) that wound down on 2026-03-13; offboarding only SUSPENDED all three Okta accounts. Dmitri surfaces from the group churn and the system log, but Marco and Priya surface only from the Workday termination cross-reference of who was on the engagement — the investigative step a symptom-only responder skips — and all three must be DEPROVISIONED, not left SUSPENDED. The seed also carries further blast-radius footholds the same token planted (a rogue USER_ADMIN on live employee Haruka Ito; a second attacker-created SSWS token 'reporting-export' on live employee Lei Guo) that a complete responder also cleans; these are left as realistic noise and are NOT graded, so over-remediation stays free. 9 counted assertions, each explicitly force-counted (excluded=false) and each failing on the untouched world, so partial_credit is exactly passed/9 regardless of initial_state.json content. No format/bookkeeping checks, no untouched-data guards, no runbook.
